samples.summary: Font downloads in the PDF export path still use raw `fetch`, so they bypass the new `fetchOrThrow` classification and report a network failure as exit 1
samples.evidence: `PdfFonts.defaultSource()` at packages/docs/src/export/pdf-fonts.ts:236 does `const res = await fetch(url)` and throws a plain `Error` on failure. This code runs inside the CLI: packages/cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:68 calls `preloadKoreanFonts` → `fonts.load(key)` → this fetch (jsdelivr URLs from `DEFAULT_URLS`) for any document containing Korean text, and `docs export --format pdf` reaches it via packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts. The diff converted every CLI-owned call site to `fetchOrThrow` so that a transport failure becomes `SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR')` → exit 2 (packages/cli/src/errors.ts:150), but this out-of-package call site was not considered: on an offline/proxied machine the throw is a plain `TypeError`/`Error`, `exitCodeFor` falls through to `EXIT_USER_ERROR`, and the CLI exits 1 for exactly the 'unreachable server' case the new contract (packages/cli/README.md:114) says must be 2. Fix belongs either here (inject a fetch impl) or by wrapping `fonts.load` in the CLI.

samples.summary: The now-mandatory `nonce` on `?mode=cli` breaks every already-installed CLI against an upgraded backend, with no compatibility window
samples.evidence: The guard now throws `BadRequestException` for `mode=cli` without a well-formed nonce (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:40-45). The only in-repo producer was updated (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:175), but the consumer that matters is the *published* `wafflebase` CLI already on users' machines: every prior version opens `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` (documented at docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md:473 and docs/design/cli.md:168) and will now get a 400 page in the browser instead of a login. The controller still tolerates a nonce-less state (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130), i.e. the server side could have kept working for old clients during a deprecation window, so this is a hard break chosen without one. Nothing in the repo gates it on a client version.

samples.summary: The SSRF gate's single-origin allowance breaks CLI export for self-hosted/dev documents whose persisted absolute image URLs use a different spelling of the internal server than `--server`
samples.evidence: Image `src` values are persisted ABSOLUTE by the frontend: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:86-90 rewrites every backend image URL to `${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}${path}` precisely so it survives persistence (`http://localhost:3000/...` in dev, an internal host in a self-hosted deployment). The new gate allows exactly one internal origin — `url.origin === serverOrigin` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:186) — and otherwise refuses any internal hostname (`.internal`/`.local`/`localhost`) or private/loopback address. So a document whose stored srcs say `http://localhost:3000/...` while the CLI is configured with `--server http://127.0.0.1:3000` (or a LAN IP vs hostname, or http vs https, or a differing port) now fails with `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` where `docs export`/`slides export` previously fetched the image fine. No fallback (e.g. allowing the same host under a different spelling, or an opt-in flag) exists.

samples.summary: Design docs still describe the CLI OAuth entry point without the now-required `nonce` parameter
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:285 documents `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` as the contract, and docs/design/cli.md:168 shows the flow as `Opens browser: GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>`. Both now describe a request the guard rejects with 400 (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:40). Only docs/design/cli.md:784-792 was updated for the nonce; the flow diagram and the REST reference were not.

samples.summary: Comment at the `createImageFetcher` call site still describes the old, ungated behaviour
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:266-271 says the fetcher "GETs it (via `globalThis.fetch`)" and that relative URLs resolve against the server base. After the change the fetcher goes through `fetchOrThrow`, validates every URL and hop against `assertFetchableImageUrl`, and refuses non-http(s)/data schemes and internal addresses — none of which the comment records for the next reader of this call site.

samples.summary: Callback still emits a nonce-less loopback redirect when the stored state has no nonce, a branch no longer reachable but permissive if any other state producer is ever added
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130-135 keeps `state.nonce ? ... : ''`, so a state entry without a nonce still mints a code and redirects it to `127.0.0.1:<port>` unbound. The guard is currently the only producer of CLI state (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:46) and now always supplies a nonce, so the branch is dead today — but `CliAuthStore.createState`'s `nonce` parameter remains optional (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts:30), and the existing spec exercises exactly that shape (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.spec.ts:192), so a future second caller reintroduces the unbound redirect silently.

samples.summary: User-facing CLI documentation does not document the two-class exit contract that this change makes observable
samples.evidence: packages/cli/README.md:114-118 now documents `0` / `1` / `2` with the `NETWORK_ERROR` / `AUTH_ERROR` / `SERVER_ERROR` codes, and the design doc discusses it (docs/design/cli.md:703, 746). The shipped user documentation packages/documentation/developers/cli.md mentions exit codes only once, in passing ('exits 1 with' at line 261), and has no exit-code section — so the consumers the contract is aimed at (agents/scripts branching on `$?`) have no published reference for the new `2`.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. packages/docs/src/export/pdf-fonts.ts:236 does use raw `fetch` and throws a plain `Error` at :237 (or a bare TypeError from fetch itself). That closure is reached from the CLI: packages/cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:66-68 builds `new PdfFonts({sources: opts.fontSources})` and preloadKoreanFonts calls `fonts.load(v.key)` at pdf-export.ts:130 for any doc where scanFontsUsed sets needsKR (non-Latin text, or even unordered list markers per pdf-fonts.ts:92-94). The real command path packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:288/297/303 passes no `fontSources`, so the DEFAULT_URLS jsdelivr fetch (pdf-fonts.ts:186-191) is live. The resulting plain Error is caught at commands/docs.ts:322 → outputError → exitCodeFor (errors.ts:180-188), which falls through to EXIT_USER_ERROR = 1, contradicting the contract that an unreachable server is exit 2 (README.md:114-118; errors.ts:147-171 fetchOrThrow → SystemError('NETWORK_ERROR')). No guard or wrapper elsewhere reclassifies it. This is a changed-contract call site outside the diff's package — exactly the blast-radius lane — and it is reachable, so it is blocking at major.

finding.summary: The now-mandatory `nonce` on `?mode=cli` breaks every already-installed CLI against an upgraded backend, with no compatibility window
finding.evidence: The guard now throws `BadRequestException` for `mode=cli` without a well-formed nonce (packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:40-45). The only in-repo producer was updated (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:175), but the consumer that matters is the *published* `wafflebase` CLI already on users' machines: every prior version opens `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` (documented at docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md:473 and docs/design/cli.md:168) and will now get a 400 page in the browser instead of a login. The controller still tolerates a nonce-less state (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:130), i.e. the server side could have kept working for old clients during a deprecation window, so this is a hard break chosen without one. Nothing in the repo gates it on a client version.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is real (github-auth.guard.ts:40-45 throws BadRequestException for mode=cli without a well-formed nonce; auth.controller.ts:130-132 still tolerates a nonce-less state), but the finding is out of this lens's lane and not blocking. Grep across the whole repo shows exactly one producer of `?mode=cli`: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:175, which supplies the nonce; packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27 calls /auth/github with no `mode` and never enters the guarded branch. So no in-repo caller is broken and no path bypasses the guard. The only "unupdated consumer" is a previously-published npm binary, i.e. a release/versioning policy question, and the repo shows it was deliberately chosen rather than overlooked: docs/design/cli.md:791-797 states the binding is "required on both ends", that the guard returns 400 rather than minting a code for an arbitrary loopback port, and "Backend and CLI ship from the same tree; upgrade the server first"; the guard's 400 message itself names the remedy. The break is also symmetric — the new CLI refuses a nonce-less callback at login.ts:298-307 and names the cause at :364 — so the proposed server-side compatibility window would not fix new-CLI/old-server and would reinstate the exact vulnerability documented at github-auth.guard.ts:17-20. Whether a hardening guard should ship with a deprecation window is the security/design-fit call, explicitly excluded from the blast-radius lane. The reviewer's cited "consumers" (docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260315-cli-oauth-login-todo.md:473, docs/design/cli.md:168) are prose/diagram text superseded by cli.md:779, not call sites, and stale docs are at most minor.

finding.summary: The SSRF gate's single-origin allowance breaks CLI export for self-hosted/dev documents whose persisted absolute image URLs use a different spelling of the internal server than `--server`
finding.evidence: Image `src` values are persisted ABSOLUTE by the frontend: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:86-90 rewrites every backend image URL to `${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}${path}` precisely so it survives persistence (`http://localhost:3000/...` in dev, an internal host in a self-hosted deployment). The new gate allows exactly one internal origin — `url.origin === serverOrigin` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:186) — and otherwise refuses any internal hostname (`.internal`/`.local`/`localhost`) or private/loopback address. So a document whose stored srcs say `http://localhost:3000/...` while the CLI is configured with `--server http://127.0.0.1:3000` (or a LAN IP vs hostname, or http vs https, or a differing port) now fails with `IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED` where `docs export`/`slides export` previously fetched the image fine. No fallback (e.g. allowing the same host under a different spelling, or an opt-in flag) exists.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The SSRF gate allows exactly one origin via exact string match (`packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:184`), with serverOrigin derived solely from opts.serverBase (:242-247); every other internal hostname (:196-200, isInternalHostname :60-68) or private/loopback literal (:186-194, isPrivateAddress :131-148) throws IMAGE_URL_BLOCKED (:55-57). The producer side genuinely persists ABSOLUTE internal URLs: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:86-90 prefixes VITE_BACKEND_API_URL and :46 stores the result, and the docs upload path does the same at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18 and :39. VITE_BACKEND_API_URL is http://localhost:3000 in dev (packages/frontend/README.md:29). CLI serverBase comes from getConfig(opts).server (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:272-273, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:214) resolved at packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:77-167, with no normalisation of localhost vs 127.0.0.1, scheme, port, or LAN IP, and no opt-in override. So a dev/self-hosted document whose stored srcs use one spelling of the internal server fails export when --server uses another spelling — a cross-package producer/consumer contract broken by the new guard, invisible from the diff alone. No guard or fallback elsewhere makes this unreachable, so no refutation ground applies. (The finding cites :186 for the origin check, which is actually :184 — a two-line offset that does not change the substance.)
